title: 187. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Representing Linear Inequality Solutions on Number Lines
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Representing a Strict Inequality on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Match the inequality \(x>2\) with its number-line representation.
questions.question: Which description matches the number-line graph of \(x>2\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Open circle at \(2\), shading to the right

options.label: B
options.text: Closed circle at \(2\), shading to the right

questions.explanation: The inequality \(x>2\) includes all numbers greater than \(2\), but it does not include \(2\) itself. On a number line, an open circle at \(2\) shows that \(2\) is excluded, and shading to the right shows all numbers greater than \(2\). Therefore, the correct description is A.
questions.hint: Decide whether \(2\) itself satisfies the inequality, and on which side of \(2\) the solutions lie.

questions.concept: Representing a Non-Strict Inequality on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Match the inequality \(x\le -1\) with its number-line representation.
questions.question: Which description matches the number-line graph of \(x\le -1\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Open circle at \(-1\), shading to the left

options.label: B
options.text: Closed circle at \(-1\), shading to the left

questions.explanation: The inequality \(x\le -1\) includes \(-1\) itself and all numbers less than \(-1\). A closed circle at \(-1\) shows that \(-1\) is included, and shading to the left shows all numbers less than \(-1\). Therefore, the correct description is B.
questions.hint: Check whether \(-1\) itself satisfies the inequality; that decides how the endpoint is drawn.

questions.concept: Reading an Inequality from a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the inequality represented by an open circle and left shading.
questions.question: A number line has an open circle at \(3\) and shading to the left. Which inequality is represented?
questions.explanation:
An open circle at \(3\) means that \(3\) is not included. Shading to the left means the solution includes values less than \(3\). Therefore, the number line represents
\[
x<3
\]
Thus, the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Ask two questions: is \(3\) itself part of the solution, and are the shaded values smaller or larger than \(3\)?

questions.concept: Representing a Double Inequality on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Match the compound inequality \(-2\le x<4\) with its number-line representation.
questions.question: Which description represents the solution of \(-2\le x<4\) on a number line?

options.label: A
options.text: Closed circle at \(-2\), open circle at \(4\), shading between them

options.label: B
options.text: Open circle at \(-2\), closed circle at \(4\), shading between them

questions.explanation: The inequality \(-2\le x<4\) includes \(-2\) because of the \({\le}\) symbol, but it does not include \(4\) because of the \({<}\) symbol. Therefore, the number line should have a closed circle at \(-2\), an open circle at \(4\), and shading between the two points. Thus, the correct description is A.
questions.hint: Check which endpoint is included and which endpoint is excluded.

questions.concept: Reading a Non-Strict Inequality from a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the inequality represented by a closed circle and right shading.
questions.question: A number line has a closed circle at \(5\) and shading to the right. Which inequality is represented?
questions.explanation:
A closed circle at \(5\) means that \(5\) is included. Shading to the right means the solution includes all numbers greater than \(5\). Therefore, the number line represents
\[
x\ge 5
\]
Thus, the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Decide whether the endpoint \(5\) itself belongs to the shaded set, then choose the inequality symbol that matches.

questions.concept: Solving and Graphing a Linear Inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(2x+1<7\) and match its solution to a number-line graph.
questions.question: Solve \(2x+1<7\). Which number-line description represents the solution?

options.label: A
options.text: Open circle at \(3\), shading to the right

options.label: B
options.text: Open circle at \(3\), shading to the left

questions.explanation:
Solve the inequality:
\[
2x+1<7 \implies 2x<6 \implies x<3
\]
The solution is all numbers less than \(3\), so the number line has an open circle at \(3\) and shading to the left. Therefore, the correct description is B.
questions.hint: Solve the inequality first, then decide the circle type and shading direction.

questions.concept: Solving and Graphing an Inequality with a Negative Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(-3x\ge 6\) and match its solution to a number-line graph.
questions.question: Solve \(-3x\ge 6\). Which number-line description represents the solution?

options.label: A
options.text: Closed circle at \(-2\), shading to the right

options.label: B
options.text: Closed circle at \(-2\), shading to the left

questions.explanation:
Divide both sides by \(-3\). Because the divisor is negative, reverse the inequality sign:
\[
x\le -2
\]
The solution includes \(-2\), so use a closed circle at \(-2\), and shade to the left. Therefore, the correct description is B.
questions.hint: Remember to reverse the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number.

questions.concept: Solving and Graphing a Linear Inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(4-x>1\) and match its solution to a number-line graph.
questions.question: Solve \(4-x>1\). Which number-line description represents the solution?

options.label: A
options.text: Open circle at \(3\), shading to the left

options.label: B
options.text: Open circle at \(3\), shading to the right

questions.explanation:
Solve the inequality:
\[
4-x>1 \implies -x>-3 \implies x<3
\]
The solution is all numbers less than \(3\), so the number line has an open circle at \(3\) and shading to the left. Therefore, the correct description is A.
questions.hint: Isolate \(x\), and remember to reverse the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

questions.learningObjective: Match \(x<-1\) or \(x\ge 2\) with its number-line representation.
questions.question: Which number-line description represents \(x<-1\) or \(x\ge 2\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Open circle at \(-1\), shading left; open circle at \(2\), shading right

options.label: B
options.text: Open circle at \(-1\), shading left; closed circle at \(2\), shading right

questions.explanation: The inequality \(x<-1\) uses an open circle at \(-1\) and shading left. The inequality \(x\ge 2\) includes \(2\), so it uses a closed circle at \(2\) and shading right. Because the compound inequality uses "or," both shaded regions are part of the solution. Therefore, the correct description is B.
questions.hint: Match each part of the compound inequality with the correct circle type and shading direction.

questions.concept: Reading a Compound Inequality from a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the compound inequality represented by a closed circle, an open circle, and shading between them.
questions.question: A number line has a closed circle at \(-3\) and an open circle at \(1\), with shading between them. Which compound inequality is represented?
questions.explanation:
A closed circle at \(-3\) means that \(-3\) is included. An open circle at \(1\) means that \(1\) is not included. Shading between them means the solution is all numbers between \(-3\) and \(1\). Therefore, the compound inequality is
\[
-3\le x<1
\]
Thus, the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: The circle type at each endpoint tells whether the inequality uses \({\le}\) or \({<}\).
